disclaimer: Typical state-level values — site-specific design values (IRC Table R301.2(1), filled in by the local jurisdiction) govern; verify with the AHJ. Entries AL through MO + DC were reconstructed on 2026-08-13 after the climate-a research output was lost; see per-entry "caveat". CA-* unit conversions: ground snow Ss kPa → psf at 1 kPa = 20.885 psf; frost depth mm → in at 25.4 mm = 1 in — documented per row in snowNote/frostLineNote.

CA-ON-E.seismicNote: The western Quebec / Ottawa Valley zone is the second-highest seismic hazard in Canada; Sa(0.2) approaches the NBC 9.23.13 prescriptive threshold and engineered lateral design may be required.

CA-ON-N.seismicNote: Low hazard across the Canadian Shield.

CA-BC.name: Canada · British Columbia
CA-BC.frostLineNote: Lower Mainland and Vancouver Island ~450 mm (18 in) in a mild marine climate. The Interior (Kamloops, Prince George) runs 1200-1800 mm — override for interior sites.
CA-BC.snowNote: Coastal Ss ~1.5-2.0 kPa (~31-42 psf); interior and mountain sites far higher.
CA-BC.windNote: Exposed coastal sites higher; no hurricane regime.
CA-BC.seismicNote: Cascadia subduction zone — the highest seismic hazard in Canada. Coastal BC exceeds the NBC 9.23.13 prescriptive bracing threshold, so Part 4 engineered lateral design is normal practice.
CA-BC.caveat: Canadian entry (added 2026-08-15): typical provincial values derived from NBC 2020 Division B Appendix C, and Ontario MMAH Supplementary Standard SB-1 for the Ontario rows. Site-specific values from the authority having jurisdiction govern. BC also enforces the BC Energy Step Code, which commonly drives thicker or double-stud exterior walls than this profile assumes.

CA-AB.seismicNote: Low hazard; the southwestern foothills are moderate.

CA-SK.name: Canada · Saskatchewan

CA-SK.seismicNote: Among the lowest seismic hazards in North America.
